title: readPLY
body:
## readPLY

Imports one polygon mesh from a PLY file with Blender's PLY importer, multiplying coordinates by scale and keeping the file's axes (Y forward, Z up, scene units ignored); other importer options keep Blender's defaults. PLY carries no unit information, so scale converts units. Point-only PLY files are rejected because the mesh must have faces.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- A point cloud PLY fails with UNSUPPORTED_RESOURCE; mesh it elsewhere first.
- scale is a constant set at creation; it cannot vary with an $axis.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `readPLY`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | Path of the PLY file to import. Relative paths are resolved against the working directory of the Schemaxis process; in workflows an $artifact from a verified producer is usual. The file is copied into the run directory and both copies are digest-checked; it is fixed when the node is created. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1}` | **required** |
| `scale` | Uniform factor applied to every imported coordinate (importer global_scale; scene units ignored). PLY stores bare numbers, so this is how you set units: 0.001 makes a millimetre export metre-sized, 1 keeps the numbers. | `{"type":"number","minimum":1e-06,"maximum":1000000}` | `1` |

- `file` is a constructor option.
- `scale` is a constructor option.
